findings.title: Single-channel stream crashes with bare IndexError at first redraw
findings.description: A stream whose samples are scalars (or length-1 vectors) -- e.g. one physiological signal or a 1-channel LSL device -- crashes as soon as the first post-head chunk is drawn: head_red has one column, is3d is False, and _redraw calls artist.set_data(full[:, 0], full[:, 1]) (streaming.py:264). Static hyp.plot of the same 1-D data works fine (plots against the index), and a head-only 1-channel stream (stream shorter than stream_init) also works, so the crash only fires once real streaming begins -- the worst time. No validation or fallback exists for n_features < 2.
findings.expected: A 1-D trajectory plotted against sample index (like static hyp.plot of the same values), or a clear ValueError up front stating streams need >= 2 features.

findings.title: Undocumented frozen-box clamping flattens post-head samples onto the display box -- visibly distorts the project's own iris tutorial example (100/150 points clamped)
findings.description: plot_stream freezes the centering/scaling affine from the first stream_init samples and CLAMPS every later sample to the [-1,1] box surface (streaming.py:226-239). Whenever the stream distribution shifts after the head -- the norm in streaming settings -- the display piles samples into straight bands on the box walls while fig.stream_info['xform_data'] keeps the true values, so the plot silently misrepresents the data. The shipped tutorial streaming_data.ipynb cell 10 (iris, stream_init=50) hits this: the head is 50 setosa rows, and ALL 100 versicolor/virginica samples land outside the frozen box (measured: 100 of 150 clamped) and render as a dense straight band along the top box edge -- fake structure, and the real two-cluster structure (visible in a static plot of the same 150 rows) is destroyed. No user-facing doc mentions clamping: the behavior is described only in internal comments/plot_stream docstring; hyp.plot docstring (stream_* params) and both streaming tutorials are silent. Also visible as flattened segments along the frame edges in the 2-channel run (v1b_2channel.png).
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('scikit-learn/iris', split='train', streaming=True)
ds = ds.select_columns(['SepalLengthCm', 'SepalWidthCm', 'PetalLengthCm', 'PetalWidthCm'])
fig = hyp.plot(ds, '.', markersize=6, stream_init=50, stream_chunk=25, show=False)
fig.savefig('/tmp/iris_streamed.png')
"  # top-edge band = 100 clamped samples
findings.expected: Either the post-head samples remain faithfully placed (e.g. axes rescale or clamping is clearly disclosed in hyp.plot docs + tutorials), or at least a runtime warning when a large fraction of streamed samples is being clamped.

findings.title: Any mid-stream error (LSL source death, NaN sample, source exception) loses the figure, ALL consumed data, and the entire animation file
findings.description: plot_stream catches only KeyboardInterrupt (streaming.py:291); writer.finish() (line 294) and the fig.stream_info attachment are skipped on any other exception, and the figure is never returned. Demonstrated three ways, all real: (a) REAL LSL outlet that stops publishing mid-plot -> lsl_stream's HypertoolsIOError propagates out of hyp.plot; the 300 already-consumed samples and the partially-streamed GIF are unrecoverable -- with PillowWriter the file doesn't exist at all (frames are buffered in memory until finish()); (b) a generator raising RuntimeError mid-stream -- same total loss; (c) a single NaN sample -> IncrementalPCA.transform raises sklearn's 'Input X contains NaN' -> same total loss. For the flagship use case (long live acquisitions) this means an amp hiccup at minute 29 of 30 destroys everything. Contradicts the hyp.plot docstring claim that any animation being saved "is finalized whenever streaming stops (including on interrupt)" (plot.py ~line 997): true for Ctrl-C (verified), false for error stops.
findings.expected: On a source error: finalize the animation, attach stream_info (with the consumed data) to the figure, and either return the figure with a warning or re-raise an exception that still references the partial results -- matching the documented "finalized whenever streaming stops" contract.
findings.actual: REAL LSL run (L10): 'HypertoolsIOError propagated: "LSL stream (name='AuditDies-82230') stopped delivering samples: nothing received for ~2.0s. The source may have disconnected." | figure+300 consumed samples LOST, gif exists=False'. Generator run (E18): RuntimeError propagated; gif size=-1 (never created); figure/stream_info LOST. NaN run (E12): ValueError: Input X contains NaN. IncrementalPCA does not accept missing values...

findings.title: Most hyp.plot kwargs are silently dropped for streaming inputs (hue, legend, animate, ...) while align/cluster raise
findings.description: The stream dispatch (plot.py:1546-1554) forwards only a fixed whitelist (fmt, stream_*, ndims, reduce, normalize, align, cluster, save_path, show, frame_rate, markersize, linewidth, color, palette, title, size, elev, azim, ax). Every other documented plot() parameter -- hue=, legend=, animate=, labels=, explore=, surface=, etc. -- is accepted without any warning and silently ignored for streams (verified for hue/animate/legend: no warnings emitted, no legend rendered). findings.title: lsl_stream docstring omits the mid-stream silence abort: timeout is documented only as resolve wait, but iteration also raises HypertoolsIOError after ~timeout seconds without samples
findings.description: The timeout parameter doc (lsl.py:52-56) and the Raises section (lsl.py:69-73) describe only the resolve-time behavior ('If no matching stream is found within timeout seconds'), but the returned generator ALSO aborts with HypertoolsIOError after ~timeout seconds of consecutive silence (verified: 81 real samples delivered, outlet stalls, next() raises after 2.0s with a good message). Consumers wrapping iteration need to know next() can raise; the behavior itself is good, just undocumented (only an inline comment, lsl.py:107-109).
findings.expected: timeout/Raises docs also state: the generator raises HypertoolsIOError if no sample arrives for ~timeout seconds mid-stream.
findings.actual: Verified behavior: received 81 real samples, then HypertoolsIOError after 2.0s of silence (timeout=2.0): LSL stream (name='AuditSilent2-83431') stopped delivering samples: nothing received for ~2.0s. The source may have disconnected.

findings.title: lsl_stream discards LSL timestamps, offers no inlet tuning, and silently picks the first of multiple matching streams
findings.description: pull_sample returns (sample, timestamp) but the timestamp is dropped (lsl.py:117) with no option to keep it -- time-synchronization is the core point of LSL for scientists; there is no way to pass StreamInlet options (max_buflen, processing_flags for clock correction); and when several streams match the criterion the first resolved one is used with no warning (verified with two same-type outlets: silently picked one of them, order not user-controlled).
findings.expected: e.g. lsl_stream(..., timestamps=True) yielding (vector, t) pairs, **inlet_kwargs passthrough, and a warning naming all matches when more than one stream resolves.
findings.actual: ('2 matches, silently picked', 'AuditMultiA-82230', '| 2 inlets on one outlet, both contiguous', True)
